Content: Connection, integrity, and solidarity are centered because it is clear that the 'culture of outrage' that currently exists led to collapse and destruction and this future thriving depends on affirming life.
Remembering the "collapse" - a sense of how collapse required much letting go of our notions of how things "should be."

We came to understand that - just as boats tack into wind to make a turn - we need to move with enough force and clarity of purpose. We were not afraid of slowing down - but we did not limit our strategies or choices out of hesitation and indecision.
This gift, that of joy and wonder even in hardship and strain, supports the creation of building what we have needed.
There is still suffering, there is still pain. But we know that some of it is simply about living.

We learned to fight for beauty, creation and wholeness, not just rights. After the great collapse some people forgot and others remembered. The "isms" people in 2024 focused on were forgotten, they are surprising things that are only referred to in history books or found by archeological research. When you dig through the history books, you see that people fought for something they couldn't fully envision, liberation or freedom or sovereignty. What these words meant in 2024, don't mean the same things in 100-150 years. But the memory of these fights provides warning to at least some of 2024's descendants to not take life for granted.
"We are the people who" share and value these. We created spaces and gatherings where we could experience a taste of this.
In 2024, we felt the tenderness of knowing that where we wanted to be was so far from where we were, but we knew that we had it within us.
We are not afraid of life. In the collapse we have lost the stability of automation and homogeneity and have stewarded comfort in our ever changing experience.

We used to be taught to pursue permanence at all costs. Before the collapse we worshipped anything or anyone who would not bend, break, or crumble. Now we understand ourselves to be more like wind and water. We do not feel sad when a building crumbles as we are taught from our earliest moments that decay is beautiful and we see how it brings forth wisdom and new life.We are taught that the human experience is seasonal. We have learned how to care for our bodies, minds and spirit and one another.
Now we have a bigger ocean of what our people were already doing. What earth had already been doing.

A memory that we knew in 2024 that the ingredients for the things that were being dreamed - visions of safety, connection, community, learning, loving, being, play - were things we already had access to then.

Old and deep pains of separation and oppression have been and continue to be alchemized - the pain transforming to ignite the possibilities for connection, courage, and camaraderie. We no longer push people into hiding and have interrupted familial repression.
We are present to our minds, spirits, bodies, and each other
We have recovered our collective sense of reverence for the world, the earth, the other beings, the air, the water, the rocks, the land, the interdependence is acknowledged and remembered.

We talked about how this circle is linked to horizon circles happening in many places to build a collective horizon. We talked about identifying the tipping point towards this collective horizon, when the thriving becomes inevitable.
Appreciate that we're starting in the dream space. Being technicians/strategists can sometimes strip us of our ability to dream.

We lost a lot of people because they had to labor outside in dangerous heat, because our water became scarce and what remained was contaminated, because Al took more jobs and because our education system didn't prepare enough people in time for new jobs. We lost people to raging seas and skies...

A memory of the hope/faith we had in 2024 - the image of a "Noah's Arc"-like vessel on the vast ocean, at the time/place when the dove was flying back with an olive branch from some land, proof of life, proof that the flood waters that had caused complete destruction had started to recede. There was hope for survival, a future. Since land wasn't in sight yet, it would still require faith to continue on the journey.
Collapse is not dystopia, despite what the media told us.

We trust our collective connection towards a collective good. More beautiful still, time reveals a natural mending and all the wisdom we need. There is reciprocal nourishment in my circle and then, a knowing that all circles I’m not in are also practicing reciprocal nourishment.
We will know our dystopian stories were just one stopping point on our pathway to thriving.

Plastic pollution and carbon and greenhouse gas emissions have been dealt with because science combined with knowledge to become wisdom to allow us to deal with the hard stuff that crippled us before. The rate of disfiguration and disease slowed and reversed amongst living beings. Our trajectory of decline was mended. Melting of ice and exposing of permafrost was slowed, and future pandemics were avoided because they were never exposed from under the ice.
To be the ancestors of Lahaina at the time of the wildfire, the time of the collapse would be cause for celebration.

Because half of the world’s population died in the collapse, due to a lack of access to medicines and acute care, medical professionals are compelled to return to natural and indigenous traditional medicines to augment western science which results in the founding of a global center for natural sciences.

Stories will be told about ancestors 150 years ago who were still experiencing the life cycle in daily life.  That daily connection with earth, water, and life made possible an understanding of the consequences of a system disconnected from natural rhythms of life and death.

Date/Circle Name: 2/1/25 St Louis Park, MN BIPOC The Coven
Content: We are recovering from the rule of force and power. Protection, support, leadership, direction are rooted in the tree ancestors’ ways of intercombination. The tree of life is a presence in so many of our ways of knowing. We would never blame them for the burning of cities or creating of litter that used to inconvenience us.

Repair and grief:  There is a sharing of the history of the collapse that holds multiple realities.  Connecting to and telling the stories of multiple interconnected lineages are the pathway to our wholeness.
Stories of loss and grief are not shrouded in secrecy but memorialized in forests and other places where they can be seen and known.

This collapse is so heavy.
There is a lot of death here–sad and beautiful.
After the collapse, people would at first live in smaller communities again until communication can be reestablished on a larger level.

Everyone understands the before. We have gone through a Truth and Reconciliation process. Everyone understands the collapse and the signs and signals of it. The mistakes of the past that almost wiped everyone out feed interdependence, mutuality and a higher level of consciousness. Lots of things are understood in different ways. Matriarchal and child-centered. Children are beloved and safe.

We are grateful for the collapse, its teachings and the space it has provided us to create together. Trying, persisting, living still requires great effort, but we come to our work as humans rested, enthusiastic and ready.
We acknowledge and remember the intense harms - greed, enslavement, genocide.  We learn and embrace the joyful world that we are in.
Despite the wisdom of Ancestor Gil Scott-Heron, he had one part wrong. The revolutions were televised, every painstaking and gory moment.

After the collapse darkness held near to us all and from that darkness a small light began to emerge from the hearts of those who remain. That small light, barely more than a flame from a candle, was fueled by love and understanding through a shared relationship with loss and pain and a recognition of what all those remained had endured together.
As we began to see the light in one another (anew) our Flames grew ever so slightly but enough to shed Light On A New Path forward.

We understood that in order to survive in order to keep that flame alive we had to stay close. as We begin to gather our shared light. We began to illuminate new ways of being, new realizations of shared spirit.
There aren't as many of us left on the planet. Those left, in deep love, offer gratitude and begin with gratitude for all of our ancestors, even those that were complicit in the destruction.
Some of it may still be here-even if we are not.
The kingdom will have collapsed.  Air quality would have gotten really bad.  Cities will have been on fire.  We will still remember that even though things are better.

After the collapse people have to come together with who they love and trust to build communities based on returning to ways of life where we feel ourselves connected to land and non-human beings. There is a flow that takes us through each day. No fear of unexpected violence or our neighbors. We know the ways of life that lead to more life. We share stories of what we have learned to ensure our communities can survive. Inner work and resources needed to maintain – humility, inner strength, calmness, slowness and time in abundance.

Too much was driven by hunger for capital, resources, power, and extending life beyond natural lifespans – mostly by an alliance of mostly men who decided to behave like gods ● The development of the dominant ‘’Big Tech’’ extracted so much, it brought us to our knees. There were many dark hours. Drastic inequality fed an appetite for rebellion . . . and something more. It made us face what it means to be human. 
● After global societal collapse in 2035, new systems of “work,” education, and incentives began to emerge once mass unemployment swept through the world without supporting systems of public welfare. 
● Massive public pressure arose, probably driven by automation and job losses as more and more people became clear that it was not a default that they/we would be part of the future being written by Big Tech. 
● Mounting pressure led to socioeconomic changes, because the few people owning tech + resources + power began to also see that the current setup is unsustainable even for them.

Capitalism had almost eaten itself. It’s near creation of the perfect proletariat ended up illuminating the obvious foil; the everyday person’s wealth was what filled the wealthiest’s bank accounts. 
There was a global re-organization like we had never seen before. The tech oligarchs who had made untold billions were forced to pay into a fund that was to generate AI that encompassed a set of values that honored the inherent dignity and values of all peoples and the planet. 
Capitalism didn’t fully collapse - but a different manifestation was cultivated. Business allows for a competence of the human spirit so long as it doesn’t become an unfettered cancer. With AI stable and in check (its exponential growth was long ago & research was more on its latent effects than its future development), the goal of any community (and communities of communities) is now on homeostasis, balance, and thriving. 
Billionaires are rare. We took a pause on trillionaires. 
We had to and still have to disrupt notions of what ‘’wealth’’ really is.
Human empires collapse, octopus councils rise, guiding humanity to restructure its existence around oceanic wisdom and reciprocity. 🐙
The food is shared with those traveling in as well as stories about what generations from a long time ago survived - how they got through the collapse and what was learned.

Collapse - this is exciting because, while there is mourning, there’s a rebuilding. A lot of nature, water and trees. Collective stewardship is taking care of things differently. Different characteristics of 7 generations. The rebuild includes those  outside of circles that created the horizon.
Empires last 250 years and the US has reached 250!

Roles for those helping collapse come faster, and protecting others from the collapse leads to learning the relationships between those peoples. That learning is important to seeing conflict as generative and destruction as generative. Unity isn’t necessarily required for collectivity.
We embrace the fact that change was and is absolutely necessary to evolve.  We tell stories of the collapse, and why it was necessary.  We are rooted in nature.
Collapse has created the conditions for possibilities to finally be endless.  We let love and art create the roles and laws.

We were like ghosts going through the world but not living. We knew we wanted something more. We yearned for community. When we thought of the future, we longed for the past we wished we had had and the present we wholeheartedly wanted.
Seven generations from now (or earlier...) the US Empire will FALL!!! NO BORDERS. NO MORE WARS. NO MORE GREED.
